study type: Secondary data analysis of cross-sectional survey data
exposure: use of radio for malaria messages
use of community health teams for malaria messages
knowledge of taking SP to prevent malaria
use of LLINS to prevent malaria
number of children the woman has
outcome: use of two or more doses of sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine (SP) for the most recent live birth
cohort: The study included 1820 women in Uganda who had recently experienced a live birth and whose data was available in the 2014 Malaria Indicator Survey.
finding: Women who knew that SP therapy was used for malaria prevention and those attended by a skilled professional at antenatal care were significantly more likely to take two or more doses of SP during pregnancy.
cross-section timing: Data was collected from the 2014 Malaria Indicator Survey dataset.
